problem: Existing VLN-CE methods learn correlations between observations and actions from training data, leading to spurious dependencies on environmental/dataset biases and poor generalization to unseen environments under domain shift.
motivation: VLN-CE agents must generalize across environmental variations and visual domain shifts. Learning observation-action correlations overfits to dataset-specific visual patterns; causal inference could let the agent learn invariant spatial structure and correct biases from prior experience.
key_idea: Use causal inference for VLN-CE: generate counterfactual style observations to learn style-invariant spatial structure (SCA), and apply causal intervention on navigation decisions to remove biases from prior experience (TCNE).
insight: From the abstract only: the claim is that counterfactual style augmentation plus causal intervention on the observation-action chain reduces reliance on environmental biases and improves generalization. No ablations or numbers are available in the provided text, so the specific contribution of each module cannot be assessed.
method: Style Causal Adjuster (SCA): generates counterfactual style observations so the agent learns invariant spatial structures rather than dataset-specific visual patterns.
Thinking Cause Navigation Engine (TCNE): applies causal intervention to adjust navigation decisions, identifying and mitigating biases from prior experience.
Observation-action chain reasoning: the model actively 'thinks' along the observation-action chain rather than passively learning from data distributions.
